# Third-party notices

The Rust application is distributed under the adjacent MIT license. The
dependency inventory below is generated from the exact locked Cargo graph;
`cargo-deny` remains the authoritative SPDX policy check.

## Slint

The user interface uses Slint 1.17 under the Slint Royalty-free Desktop,
Mobile, and Web Applications License 2.0. Public distribution must also
satisfy one of the attribution methods in section 2 of that license.

Copyright © SixtyFPS GmbH <info@slint.dev>

<https://slint.dev/>

## Whisper

Speech recognition uses OpenAI Whisper model weights and the whisper.cpp
runtime through `whisper-rs`. Model artifacts are downloaded only after a
user choice and are verified by size and SHA-256 before activation.

- OpenAI Whisper: <https://github.com/openai/whisper>
- whisper.cpp: <https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp>
- whisper-rs: <https://github.com/tazz4843/whisper-rs>

## NVIDIA CUDA runtime

The installer contains no NVIDIA files. The optional CUDA speech worker is
built from public source and links the CUDA runtime dynamically. Its NVIDIA
runtime files (`cudart64_13.dll`, `cublas64_13.dll`, `cublasLt64_13.dll`)
are downloaded from developer.download.nvidia.com inside SayFlex, only
after the user presses the download button and accepts the NVIDIA CUDA
Toolkit EULA: <https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/eula/>. SayFlex checks the
SHA-256 of every archive and file. These files are proprietary NVIDIA
software and are not covered by the SayFlex MIT license.

## Translation models

Optional translation packs and llama.cpp are downloaded only after an
explicit user choice. Exact artifacts, checksums, origins, and model licenses
are documented in `docs/THIRD_PARTY_MODELS.md`.

The compact English language-pair packages use `fxtranslate` under MPL-2.0 and
Firefox Translations v3 model artifacts under MPL-2.0. Packages are available
for Russian, Ukrainian, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Italian,
Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, and Arabic. Model
files are installed separately on demand from Mozilla, verified in compressed
and expanded form, and are not bundled in the SayFlex installer.

- fxtranslate: <https://github.com/gregtatum/translations>
- Firefox Translations: <https://github.com/mozilla/translations>

## Screen translation OCR models

Screen translation includes the PP-OCRv5 mobile ONNX detector, recognizers,
and dictionaries distributed by RapidOCR. These model artifacts are licensed
under Apache-2.0 and verified by size and SHA-256 before packaging. The shipped
bundle identity is `screen-ocr-ppocrv5-mobile-v3.9.2`; recognition is CPU-only.
HY-MT2 and other benchmark-only candidates are not shipped.

- RapidOCR: <https://github.com/RapidAI/RapidOCR>
- PaddleOCR: <https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR>

## Native components

- whisper.cpp and ggml (speech recognition, compiled into the speech workers): MIT.
- Silero VAD v6.2.0 (`speech-vad/ggml-silero-v6.2.0.bin`, voice activity detection): MIT.
- ONNX Runtime (screen-text recognition, compiled into `SayFlex.Ocr.exe`): MIT;
  its own third-party notices: <https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/main/ThirdPartyNotices.txt>.
- gemmology (int8 matrix kernel in the translation worker): MIT.
- xsimd (SIMD wrappers used by gemmology): BSD-3-Clause.
- Microsoft Visual C++ runtime (`vcruntime140*.dll`, `msvcp140*.dll`): redistributed
  unmodified under the Microsoft Visual Studio redistribution terms, which allow
  app-local deployment; it is not covered by the SayFlex MIT license.
- llama.cpp (contextual translation, MIT) is downloaded from its GitHub release only
  after the user chooses a contextual model; it is not in the installer.
